content.text:
{"prompt": "A square, purely nonrepresentational abstract painting that fills the entire canvas edge to edge, with no frame, border, wall, room, or gallery setting. Oil and cold wax on heavy canvas, built from many layers. The palette is deep ultramarine and blackened indigo, with a cool grey-green underlayer. Slashes of hot vermilion and one narrow, intense band of pale lemon-gold cut through it. Small scrapes of bone white show through from beneath.

The left two-thirds is dense and turbulent. Thick impasto knife strokes pile up in overlapping diagonals. Scumbled veils of translucent blue lie over opaque patches. Dry-brush drags leave broken, scratchy edges. Sgraffito lines are scored into wet paint so the darker layers show underneath. The strokes push against each other and make tight, crowded rhythms, as if many competing currents were being forced into a single direction.

From the center toward the upper right, the density gives way to one wide, calm field of thinly glazed, luminous grey-blue. It is almost empty, with only faint ghostly traces of earlier strokes under the surface. The vermilion gathers into one sharp, pressured seam where the turbulent mass meets this open space. The tension comes from the contrast between congestion and stillness, and from a single decisive gold stroke that is steady and unhurried.

The texture is tactile and uneven. Glossy ridges sit next to matte, chalky areas, with fine cracks, drips, and the ghosts of scraped-away marks. The gesture is energetic but controlled, with visible bodily momentum in the brushwork. The overall mood is intense, searching, and unresolved, moving toward clarity without fully arriving. No objects, figures, faces, symbols, letters, numbers, text, horizons, or scenes appear anywhere."}
